**Summary: 7 BLOCKER findings, all relating to invalid state representation:**

| # | Rule | Line | Problem |
|---|------|------|---------|
| 1 | `make_illegal_states_unrepresentable` | 3 | `status: String` — any arbitrary string is valid |
| 2 | `make_illegal_states_unrepresentable` | 4 | `is_validated: bool` — independent of status |
| 3 | `make_illegal_states_unrepresentable` | 5 | `is_sent: bool` — redundant with status, independently mutable |
| 4 | `make_illegal_states_unrepresentable` | 9 | `mark_sent` has no state-gate — accepts any input |
| 5 | `functional_core_domain_types` | 6 | `sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64>` — raw primitive, no newtype |
| 6 | `functional_core_domain_types` | 2 | `id: String` — raw primitive, no `LeaseId` newtype |
| 7 | `no_production_unsafe_or_panics` | 10 | `"sent".to_string()` string-literal state mutation |

**Root cause:** The struct has no typestate — three independent primitive fields (`String` + `bool` + `bool`) encode the same logical state, making contradictory states (e.g., `status: "draft"` with `is_sent: true`) trivially constructible and `mark_sent` has zero transition guards.
